nodes.name: enrich Endpoint
nodes.notes:
Fixed path /webhook/lp-mock-enrich.

Originally one webhook on `lp-mock/:service`. Path parameters did not register
on this n8n build - every request answered 404 while the workflow reported
active:true and an identical fixed-path webhook in LP-00 answered fine. Three
fixed paths cost two extra nodes and remove an unknown; the chaos machinery
downstream is still written once.

nodes.name: Read Counter
nodes.notes:
The call counter reuses lp_idem under scope="mock" instead of adding a ninth
table. It is the same shape - a key and an attempt count - and Data Table
schemas cannot be altered after creation, so fewer tables is fewer things to
get permanently wrong.

nodes.name: Hang Past Timeout
nodes.notes:
The caller times out at 25s, so 35s here reproduces a timeout without needing
anything to actually be broken. Deliberately longer than the gateway timeout
and shorter than the workflow one, so the execution still finishes and stays
visible in the log.

nodes.name: Respond 429
nodes.notes:
Sends a real Retry-After. The gateway prefers that header over its own
backoff curve, and this is the only place that behaviour can be exercised:
Odoo itself imposes no rate limit here, so the 429 has to be injected.

nodes.name: Respond Malformed

parameters.responseBody: Service temporarily degraded, please retry shortly.

nodes.notes:
HTTP 200, Content-Type says JSON, body is prose. This is the shape that breaks
naive integrations: the status says success, so anything keying off the status
code alone records a success and moves on with undefined fields.

nodes.name: Respond 401

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: "unauthorized", message: "Simulated bad or expired credential" }) }}

nodes.notes:
Exists to prove a negative: 401 is classified permanent, so the caller must
NOT burn three attempts on it. A dead credential retried on a backoff curve is
how a five-minute outage becomes a thirty-minute one.

parameters.content:
## LP-99 Mock Services

Stands in for the enrichment provider, WhatsApp Cloud API and the booking system.

**Its real job is failing on demand**, because that is what the 14 edge cases need:

```
?fail=timeout&times=2   times out twice, then succeeds   (EC-3)
?fail=429&times=1       one rate limit, then succeeds    (EC-6)
?fail=malformed         200 OK with prose, not JSON      (EC-4)
?fail=500 | auth        server error / dead credential
?reset=1                clears the counter for that key
```

The counter is stored, so "twice then succeeds" is genuinely reproducible rather than a claim. The WhatsApp response is shaped exactly like Meta's, so going live is a URL and a credential.
